ai_llm_rag.notes: Q22 (RAG debugging tree): good production instincts (citations/highlighting in his lawyer-doc RAG app, retry via smaller guard model for generation failures), and honestly flagged ranking/reranking as a gap rather than bluffing. But didn't name the core isolation technique (freeze retrieved context, replay it manually to bisect retrieval/ranking vs generation failure) and conflated retrieval with ranking as one step. Taught reranking/cross-encoder basics in-session. Baseline set at developing/flat -- first data point for this area.

dsa_sql.label: Practical DSA and SQL (low priority for this role, tie-breaker only)

own_projects_deep_dive.label: Ability to defend own resume claims with real numbers/architecture (Cellular, Aurora/Pulse, GeoStorm, Jio recommender, Jio ATS, RLHF dashboard)

system_design_and_architecture.notes: Can defend real scaling decisions (700 pods, vector math offload). Weaker on org-level design tradeoffs and versioning strategies.

backend_infrastructure_and_deployment.notes: Kubernetes, Postgres tuning, Redis pipelines, Kafka. Honest about pain points; would rebuild with serverless + vector DB + Go.

ownership_and_execution.notes: Sole owner of recommender, mentored juniors to SDE1. Clear on why early exits happened (funding, wrong team, contract end). Ready to defend.

career_stability_and_motivation.notes: Three short stints were circumstantial, not flaky. Problem-driven, not prestige-driven. Floor of 1yr, aiming for Staff/Architect. Prepping on AI/system design.

devops_and_cloud.notes: GCP, Kubernetes, managed services. Thinking about serverless. Hasn't shipped major multi-region or DR yet (mentioned for StatusNeo but no depth).

ai_and_ml_engineering.notes: Embedding generation + vector similarity is production ML, not deep learning. RLHF dashboard at Turing was ops-heavy. Self-aware this is a gap; actively prepping.

python_basics.notes: GIL concept solid, but missed I/O and C extension release cases. Mutable defaults nailed. Shallow/deep copy behavior reversed on nested objects — needs clarification.

python_async.notes: Not tested in detail this round; marked from prior context.

web_api_fastapi.notes: Practical FastAPI + Pydantic usage strong. Lacks architectural understanding of ASGI vs WSGI, Pydantic validation cost at scale.

caching_redis.notes: No production experience with distributed locks or Redlock. Basic Redis usage solid.

messaging_kafka.notes: Real TB-scale production experience. Understands partitioning, ordering guarantees, consumer groups. Confident and accurate.

messaging_rabbitmq.notes: Used for task queues, dead-letter patterns, fan-out. Clear on when to use vs Kafka.

containers_docker.notes: Multi-stage build concept understood, but hasn't built from scratch in 2+ years. Details hazy (wheel copying, layer optimization).

security_oauth_oidc.notes: Used once in career. Confusing OAuth2 (authorization framework) with OIDC (authentication layer). Access vs ID token distinction unclear.

skill_areas.notes: MRO/C3, metaclasses, descriptors (__getattr__, __getattribute__, __get__) all unknown. No real exposure. This is a significant gap for Staff-level Python work.

Solid on event loop concept and basics. Weak on detection of blocking in production (py-spy/yappi). gather vs TaskGroup vs as_completed unknown. Structured concurrency not practiced. Admits most codebases he joins are sync-heavy; limited real async debugging.

Error codes + Swagger docs implemented. Missing: retryability signals (4xx vs 5xx semantics, explicit field), correlation ID terminology (calls it trace ID but the concept is there). Request-scoped sessions pattern is strong — read replicas, Depends injection, transaction scoping all correct.
Fixed window and sliding window log understood. Token bucket hazy. No discussion of deployment strategy (edge vs in-app). Needs hands-on implementation.
Built from scratch at first company, pattern known but details faded. Not recently tested.
SIGTERM handling and terminationGracePeriodSeconds known. preStop hook completely unknown — identified as priority learning gap. Wants to build this pattern himself.

Job ID polling pattern solid. FastAPI background tasks vs Celery distinction clear. Broker/backend architecture, task distribution, Flower monitoring all covered in practice. Strong on queue design and scaling patterns.
